scene.testo: Walk into the Congo Basin and the jungle wins within days. Swamps swallow your legs, rivers hide crocodiles, and no road exists for hundreds of miles. We mapped Mars, yet this forest still hides secrets. Why?

In 1482, Portuguese sailors reached the Congo River's mouth. Rapids soon blocked their ships. For centuries, outsiders stayed near the coast, while the vast interior remained unmapped and unknown to Europe.

The basin covers over 1.2 million square miles of dense forest. Rivers flood, soil turns to mud, and disease thrives. Sleeping sickness and malaria killed explorers long before any road reached the heart.

In 1885, King Leopold of Belgium claimed the Congo as his private property. Rubber quotas brought terror and millions died. War followed independence in 1960, and conflict still blocks entire regions today.

Today, the Congo Basin is the planet's second-largest rainforest, home to forest elephants, gorillas and uncontacted peoples. Maybe it is not off limits to us. Maybe we are the ones who must stay careful.

descrizione:
Why is the Congo Basin still off limits to humans? Discover how swamps, rivers, disease and history built the world's most impenetrable rainforest in Central Africa.

From Portuguese sailors in 1482 to colonial terror under King Leopold and modern conflict, this short documentary explains why the Congo remains largely unmapped, and why that matters for the planet.

Watch to learn how the second-largest rainforest on Earth guards forest elephants, gorillas and secrets we are only beginning to understand.
